reasoning_checks: The claim map specifies allowed faces, asset pools, costs, recourse, equal-ranking distributions, final discharge and omitted-claim exclusions. Liquidation sales occur at date 0; continuation cash occurs exactly one year later.

Secured recovery includes collateral plus only the deficiency’s general-pool recovery. Collateral excess transfers to the general estate; sale costs are deducted once from their specified pools. The general formula has an explicit zero-eligible-claims boundary.

The small lab intentionally requires positive faces in the three debt classes and validates that domain. Its empty-estate test concerns zero net assets with positive eligible claims, not an unsupported zero-denominator contract.

Recovery divided by original face differs from realized return on historical price. The historical purchase occurs before recovery is known; no current arbitrage price or annualized performance claim is implied.

Brindle immediate uses 30 equal internal cash 10 plus new money 20. The finite restart budget covers the interval; final cash 154 excludes financial receipts/payments but is net of all subsequent operating and investment requirements. Internal cash is spent once and not added again at the end.

The certain new loan’s actual final receipt 21 is worth its issue proceeds 20. Every final receipt sums to 154 and every dated claim value sums to 440/3. Subtracting the external issue once leaves old value 380/3, compared with net liquidation 110.

The continuation priority and cancellation of unpaid claims are explicitly a proposed unanimous agreement. Favorable class values do not prove consent. The final-cash threshold 136.5 gives zero aggregate surplus but class losses under the unmodified priority; the amended 78/22.5/15 allocation restores each liquidation value.

Debt conversion divides the already valued residual after new finance. The complete 100-thousand-share cap table assigns 65/21/14 thousand shares to old creditors and zero to cancelled old common. Changes relative to the priority proposal sum to zero, and no unlisted old claim remains.

The risky revision uses an expressly risk-neutral probability law, not a general substitution of physical probabilities for risk pricing. New-debt face is solved from min(face, actual state cash). Face 21 raises only 135/7; face 22 raises 20 and leaves actual expected return 5% despite promised yield 10%.

Risky final cash exhausts all old/new claims state by state. Old secured loses 10 versus liquidation while other old classes gain only 60/7, so internal redistribution cannot make all weakly better off under the fixed negative-surplus plan.

Rillstone’s new lender advances 32 and receives none of the independent arranger’s fee 2. The loan return 2% therefore matches actual receipts/proceeds; fee treatment does not hide a discounted issue price.

The retained zero-yield reserve is released only at the final date. Initial cash and conditional proceeds meet current debt, fee and reserve exactly; later reserve plus operations pay all new debt, extended debt and common cash. No rollover or final asset is omitted.

The extension cash has the same PV as an immediate face payment at the stated certain rate. The actual no-agreement outside option is not supplied or automatically assigned full face. The unsigned branch returns no funded closing plan because the new-money commitment is also conditional.

The stipulated extra future consent payment is a transfer from equity to one creditor, not an operating loss or an inferred bargaining equilibrium. Its value is exactly 50/51. Separate fees, delay and third-party effects need separate evidence.

The lower-capacity/capped-extension exercise closes both cash dates and fairly prices the new common contribution. Increased total common cash includes a new claim: old owners still receive 21.16 after the new investor receives 2.04.

All three worked examples, eight full prompts and solutions, teach-back and delayed check were manually matched to every requested calculation, assumption, timing statement and evaluation criterion. Numerical checks supplement this audit; they do not decide legal or real governance questions.

resolved_findings.finding: The general unsecured recovery formula did not explicitly state its positive-denominator condition.
resolved_findings.resolution: Added d+B+T > 0 and the no-eligible-claim case, where the pool goes to equity with no rate. Confirmed lab already restricts all three old faces to positive amounts, and documented that smaller domain.

resolved_findings.finding: The initial wording could imply that Rillstone’s new lender received the fee while still earning only the stated 2% on gross proceeds.
resolved_findings.resolution: Manuscript, input contract and README identify an independent arranger as the fee recipient. The lender advances the full gross 32 and receives 32.64; no model inputs changed.

resolved_findings.finding: Time-compensated extension language could be read as an assumption that the no-agreement old claim already trades at full face.
resolved_findings.resolution: Clarified that the revised stream matches an immediate face payment in PV; the realizable no-agreement outside option still needs evidence and is not supplied in the refinancing case.

limitations: Contractual priority, recourse, unanimous amendment and discharge are fictional enforceable assumptions. A real restructuring requires actual law, entity boundaries, rights and professional evidence.

Supplied liquidation realizations and continuation cash are not valuations estimated from actual market evidence. The risky example’s risk-neutral pricing convention is explicit and not generally inferred from probabilities.

The finite lab has three positive old face amounts, fixed class order, stated dates, no omitted claims and complete final settlement. It is not a bankruptcy, group-consolidation or general treasury engine.

Proposed class participation and future cash adequacy do not obtain signatures, a lender commitment or intraperiod funding. The unsigned and failed-funding branches deliberately do not assert a compliant close.

The governance discussion offers scoped process recommendations and identifies missing stakeholder effects. It neither solves bargaining equilibrium nor establishes universal duties or legally compulsory distributions.
Author/agent review is not independent human certification. Coordinator acceptance follows dependencies and includes integration/publication; browser/mobile/print visual QA remains separate.
